manifest.prompt: make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component.
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 32 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=32, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' shopping-component.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' shopping-component.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' shopping-component.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' shopping-component.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' shopping-component.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: A minimal product card whose one add control feeds a mini bag that reaches checkout, with every element doing a job.

poles: targets of at least 24 px and body text at 16 px

task.is: a compact, minimal, modern shopping component: a self-contained UI element through which a shopper finds a product, chooses it and buys it
disciplines: front-end engineering (semantic HTML, CSS, small JS)
ladder: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
a compact, minimal, modern shopping component
its anatomy, spacing, type, color, states, motion and timing values

readings.reading: product card with quick add and mini bag that reaches checkout
includes: variant picker when the product has variants
quick add to bag from the card
mini bag with lines, quantity, subtotal and checkout action

readings.reading: mini bag or bag drawer only
product list with filters and sorting

routing.job: always first: the defining tier-1 entries
routing.when: pull first for any job: the most relevant entries (relevance, not rules)

routing.job: build the component end to end
routing.when: before writing markup, styles or behavior

routing.job: set the look, timing and not-wanted list for the build
routing.when: after the structure, before writing styles and motion

routing.job: review a built component against the dump
routing.when: after the component renders, before sign-off
when writing any button, status or bag text
when justifying a choice to the user

routing.job: explore the options, readings and decision points
routing.when: when the scope or a choice is still open

ak-not-meant-minimal.excluded_sense: empty or unlabeled UI; the controls the job needs left out; a bare placeholder
ak-not-meant-minimal.instead: few elements with little decoration, each doing work, and the controls the job needs present and labeled

ak-glossy-badge.instead: plain text sale tag in a solid, high-contrast chip

ak-stock-sans.instead: a system UI font stack with set weights for product name, price and meta text

ak-emoji-ornament.instead: no decorative emoji; an icon only where it carries meaning

ak-compressed-target.instead: targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px, with spacing that keeps them apart

ak-not-meant-component.instead: a self-contained, reusable UI element with its own states

ak-not-meant-shopping.excluded_sense: grocery list; shopping-mall map; a sign-in or account page. A product grid with filters and sorting is a separate reading (see readings), not the default; a browse page may reuse this component's product card
ak-not-meant-shopping.instead: the buying flow of an online store: choose, add, pay

ak-hover-only-add.instead: add control visible at all times, and reachable by keyboard and touch. A reveal on hover or focus may add a size row or a quick-add shortcut on top of a visible add control, as an option; the add control itself stays visible at rest

ak-gradient-cta.instead: flat solid-color button with a plain text label and a visible focus ring. A subtle gradient within one color role is an allowed option when the label still passes 4.5:1 contrast and the focus ring stays visible

ak-not-meant-modern.excluded_sense: retro or skeuomorphic styling (faux wood, bevels, stitched leather)
ak-not-meant-modern.instead: current web conventions: system-level CSS, flexible layout, clear type, restrained color. Soft elevation, translucent or blurred surfaces, subtle gradients and rounded corners are allowed options within that, each used with restraint

ak-icon-only-cart.instead: a visible text label beside the icon, such as Add to bag or Bag (2). An icon-only bag control is an allowed option when its accessible name states the count, such as 'Bag, 2 items' in an aria-label

ak-blocking-modal.term: modal that blocks the page on add
ak-blocking-modal.instead: inline confirmation or a non-blocking bag count update. A variant chooser may open as a dialog before the add, since the shopper chooses inside it, and the bag drawer may open from the bag button

ak-not-meant-compact.excluded_sense: cramped or crowded text; controls compressed below 24 CSS px
ak-not-meant-compact.instead: a small footprint with few parts, tight but legible spacing, and targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS px. A phone-first footprint is an allowed reading when the card still holds at desktop widths

ak-shadow-card.instead: flat card with a 1 px border or a faint tonal fill, and no shadow at rest. A soft shadow on card hover or focus is an allowed option for emphasis, as is one shadow level on the bag drawer or popover

ak-glassmorphism.instead: restrained solid surfaces and plain system-level CSS. A translucent surface or one backdrop blur is an allowed option on the bag drawer or popover, provided text contrast still passes

k-target-size.text: Pointer targets on the card and in the bag measure at least 24 by 24 CSS px.

test.spec: getBoundingClientRect of every button, swatch, stepper control and link is at least 24 x 24 px at 390 px and at desktop width

k-contrast.text: Text sits at or above the contrast minimum against its real background.

test.spec: computed text color against its effective background is at least 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text

k-focus-visible.text: Each focused control shows a visible keyboard focus indicator.

test.spec: tab through the card and the bag; every focused control shows an outline or ring visible against its background

k-reduced-motion.text: Interaction-triggered motion has a reduced-motion alternative.

test.spec: a prefers-reduced-motion block exists and removes the transform and transition used by the add feedback and the bag drawer

k-focus-path.text: Tab order follows the card's reading order, with the title link first.

test.spec: keyboard walk from the product title through the card controls to the add control, in DOM order

k-sold-out-a11y.text: A sold-out option stays focusable and announces itself as sold out.

test.spec: sold-out option carries aria-disabled and an accessible name containing 'sold out'

k-one-card.text: One card per product, not one per color or size.

test.spec: count of product cards in the markup equals the count of products

k-price-visible.text: The price stays visible on the card at rest.

test.spec: price is visible without hover, tap or open action

k-compare-at.text: A sale display shows a compare-at price higher than the current price.

test.spec: when a sale is shown, compare-at value is greater than the current value

k-compact.text: The card and bag hold only the parts the job needs, with spacing that is tight but legible.

test.spec: list the parts on the card and bag; each one is in the required set or the variant and option set

k-minimal.text: Every element on the card and bag does work; nothing decorative is added.

test.spec: each element names the task step it serves

k-modern.text: The layout uses current CSS layout and markup conventions.

test.spec: card grid uses flex or grid; no float or table layout for the grid

k-whole-job.text: The component covers the whole buying job, from the product to checkout.

test.spec: walk the job: pick, see price and variant, choose options and quantity, add, see the bag, review, check out

k-no-noise-words.text: Copy avoids the empty intensifiers 'stunning' and 'seamless'.

test.spec: no occurrence of 'stunning' or 'seamless' in component text

k-cart-label.text: The bag control carries a visible text label or an accessible name with the count.

test.spec: bag control has visible text or an aria-label that states the item count

q-framework.text: Which framework or stack, if any?
q-framework.default: plain HTML, CSS and a small amount of vanilla JS in one self-contained file

q-brand.text: Which brand, palette and product data?
q-brand.default: unbranded neutral palette and placeholder product data

q-price-paywall.text: Full guidance on price-related offers sits behind a paywall and was not read; the sale-pricing point rests on the issue statement alone.
q-price-paywall.default: keep sale, original and currency values consistent everywhere they appear
q-price-paywall.resolve: read the full guidance or accept the issue statement

q-palette-sample.text: The palette values are sampled from web page screenshots; they are not print or brand specs.
q-palette-sample.default: use the palette options as placeholders

q-confirmation-form.text: The sources read do not rank the three confirmation forms (overlay, drop-down cart, in-between page).
q-confirmation-form.default: one form, with its controls reachable by keyboard
q-confirmation-form.resolve: pick one form at build time

q-gallery-screenshot.text: The confirmation gallery screenshot is too small to read its controls, so it gives layout context only.
q-gallery-screenshot.resolve: none needed unless a visual reference is supplied

q-final-total.text: Does the bag show a final total with tax and shipping?
q-final-total.default: bag shows the subtotal and a note that tax and shipping are added at checkout

q-quantity-cap.text: Is there a maximum quantity or stock limit on the stepper?
q-quantity-cap.default: minimum 1, maximum 10 placeholder, replaced by real stock when available

q-checkout-failure.text: What happens when checkout fails or the bag is stale?
q-checkout-failure.default: show an inline error beside Checkout and keep the bag intact

q-bag-persistence.text: Does the bag survive a page reload?
q-bag-persistence.default: in-memory for the page session only, no storage

q-undo-remove.text: Can a removed bag line be restored?
q-undo-remove.default: no undo; removing is immediate and the line can be re-added

q-bag-empty-count.text: Does the bag count read 0 or hide when empty?

q-remove-label.text: What is the visible label of the remove control in the bag?
q-remove-label.default: Remove, with an accessible name that includes the item name

q-currency-format.default: Intl.NumberFormat with the page locale, tabular figures

q-dark-mode.text: Is there a dark mode palette?
q-dark-mode.resolve: add a second palette if needed

q-phone-variant.text: Is the variant picker an inline row or a bottom sheet on phones?
q-phone-variant.default: inline row that wraps at 390 px; bottom sheet only when options exceed the row

request._about: The user's own words, split into clauses. Literal; no glosses.

r-make.anchor: make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component
r-make.text: The user asks for a shopping component, made compact, minimal and modern.

r-shopping.text: The thing to make is a shopping component.

ux_principles._about: Discipline primer for the top two rungs (UX and UI design; e-commerce interfaces) as they apply to a compact, minimal, modern shopping component. Researched entries are quoted from pages fetched 2026-11-04; the rest are the builder's own reading, tier 2 at most.

ux-wcag-target-size.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA: pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px. Exceptions: spacing (24 px circles around each target do not overlap another target), inline targets, browser-controlled size, an equivalent control elsewhere on the page, and essential presentation.

ux-wcag-contrast.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (AA): text needs a contrast ratio of 4.5:1 against its background; large text (18 pt, or 14 pt bold) needs 3:1. SC 1.4.11 (AA): the visual cues that identify a control and its state (borders, icons, focus rings) need 3:1 against adjacent colors. Inactive controls are excluded. Computed ratios are compared without rounding.

ux-wcag-focus.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7 (AA): a keyboard focus indicator is visible in some mode of operation. SC 2.4.11 (AA): a focused control is not entirely hidden by author content such as a sticky header or footer. Content the user opens may cover a focused control if the user can reveal that control without moving keyboard focus.

ux-wcag-reduced-motion.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions, level AAA: motion triggered by interaction can be disabled unless the animation is essential. Sites can honor the OS or browser reduce-motion setting through the prefers-reduced-motion media query, or offer their own control for non-essential animation.

ux-law-hick.text: Hick's law: decision time grows with the number and complexity of choices. Applied here: keep the visible options few (one primary add action, a short variant set, one quantity control) and reveal extras on demand. The same page's takeaway: minimize choices when response times are critical.

ux-law-fitts.text: Fitts's law: the time to reach a target depends on its distance and inversely on its size. Applied here: make the add-to-bag and quantity controls large enough to hit in one move, keep them near the variant choices they depend on, and do not shrink them to save space (see ux-wcag-target-size).

ux-law-jakob.text: Jakob's law: users expect a site to work the way the other sites they know work. Applied here: use familiar placement for the product image, name, price, variant row, quantity stepper, add button and a bag icon with a count, in the usual order and places, rather than novel layouts.

ux-law-proximity.text: Gestalt proximity: elements placed close together read as related, and proximity can outweigh color or shape cues. Applied here: keep the price beside the name, and keep each variant control with the add action it affects. Keep unrelated controls apart, since grouping unrelated elements can camouflage them.

ux-heuristic-minimal.text: Nielsen heuristic 8, aesthetic and minimalist design: interfaces should not show information that is irrelevant or rarely needed. Applied here: each element earns its place; secondary specs, long copy and decorative chrome move to a detail view. Other Nielsen heuristics that bear on this build: visibility of system status (feedback after add) and recognition rather than recall (keep labels and the bag count visible).

ux-ecom-add-to-bag.text: Add to bag: the add control sits with the chosen variant and the selected options are shown before the press. After the press, confirm in place: the button shows a short state label (for example 'Added') for a moment, the bag count updates, and a polite live-region announcement reaches screen readers. An opening drawer interrupts; a count change does not. Disable the button only with a stated reason (no variant chosen, out of stock) and say the reason beside it.

ux-ecom-price.text: Price display: the current price is the strongest type on the card, with the compare-at price struck through beside it when on sale, the currency shown, and a tax or shipping note in smaller text. Update the price in place when a variant changes that affects it. Say 'Sale' in words beside the price, not only through color.

ux-mistakes.text: Common mistakes: icon-only controls under 24 px; focus rings removed for looks; the add control revealed only on hover, with no touch or keyboard path; an add with no confirmation, so shoppers add twice; disabled-looking buttons that are active; a sticky header covering the focused control; motion with no reduced-motion path; a price that changes after add with no sign; many options shown at once. Every control should also work from the keyboard alone (WCAG 2.1.1, from general knowledge, not fetched in this ticket).

commerce_patterns._about: Variant selector patterns from Shopify's shopify-variant-selector component docs (one fetched page). The page names the parts a selector renders (color swatch, radio option, select) and its behaviour; it does not rank the patterns or say when each fits. Every 'fits' line is an inference and says so.

options._about: options, not requirements: decision points with tradeoffs and signals. Built from the researched entries above plus general practice, marked inferred where no fetched source backs them.

dp-bag.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
dp-bag.text: Option set: drawer that slides in over the page, a bag page, or an inline summary. Tradeoff: a drawer keeps the shopper in context and is quick to dismiss; a page gives full review room but ends browsing. Signal: a single-item buy suggests going straight to checkout; a multi-item store suits a drawer. No fetched source backs the signal; general practice.

dp-add-feedback.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
dp-add-feedback.text: Option set: the button changes to a confirmed state plus the bag count rises; or the bag drawer opens on add. Tradeoff: an inline change confirms without interrupting; opening the drawer confirms strongly but interrupts. Signal: the shopper needs proof the item landed, so the count and button label change in place at minimum. No fetched source backs the signal; general practice, not verified.

opt-hover-reveal-add.text: Option: the add control appears when the card is hovered or focused, for pointer devices, and stays visible at rest for touch and keyboard users. Tradeoff: a quieter card at rest with fewer controls competing with the photo, against lower discoverability, a second code path to build and test, and a control that a pointer user has to find by hovering. The rest-visible add control is the default; this option trades some of it for density.

opt-confirm-dialog.text: Option: after add, a small dialog confirms the item and offers View bag or Keep shopping; or a variant dialog opens from the card before adding. Tradeoff: certain confirmation and a clear next step, against an interruption on every add, a focus trap to build and test, and a slower path for a repeat buyer. The default is the inline Added label with a non-blocking bag count update; a dialog fits when the product needs a choice that a card cannot hold.

dec-variant-and-cart.text: Decision points for the variant picker and the bag lines, each with a default the builder can take as is.

decisions.default: radio group of size buttons for sizes, swatches with a visible text label for colors, and a native select above eight options

options.tradeoff: fast visual scan, against low density for text labels and weak contrast on pale colors
compact and clear for two to four options, against cramped targets and wrapping as the count grows
dense and accessible for long lists, against no visual preview of the choices

decisions.decision: price and image on variant change
decisions.default: the price updates when the variant carries its own price; the image swaps to the variant's photo when one exists; a polite live region announces the new price only when it changes

options.tradeoff: simplest, against ignoring variant pricing and photos
shows the color without a price change, against a shopper who may not see a price difference

decisions.default: merge into one bag line and add to its quantity

options.tradeoff: needed for personalized items, against duplicate lines to review in the bag

options.option: merge only when nothing is personalized
options.tradeoff: keeps lines tidy for plain goods, against a rule the shopper cannot see

dp-variant.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
dp-variant.text: Option set: visible buttons for sizes, swatches for color, select for long lists. Tradeoff: buttons and swatches are fast to scan but use space and need labels; a select is dense but hides availability. Signal: a short list of sizes favors buttons; many colors favor swatches that carry a visible name.

add_confirmation._about: What happens after add-to-bag is pressed (query 6). Source page is a Baymard index of screenshots: it gives patterns and one usability finding, not a full spec. Bag contents (query 7) are not covered by this page.

cp-atc-next-goals.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-atc-next-goals.text: After an add, shoppers may keep shopping, review the bag, or go straight to checkout, and the confirmation should help them reach whichever goal they pick. Implication: the confirmation offers a clear next step for each of the three goals, not only a checkout link.

cp-atc-clear-paths.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-atc-clear-paths.text: Usability testing found that unclear or ambiguously labeled paths in the confirmation made participants waste time working out where to go. Implication: label each next step with its exact destination (for example view bag, checkout), never a vague label.

cp-atc-formats.term: confirmation as overlay, drop-down or in-between page
cp-atc-formats.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-atc-formats.text: The confirmation can take three forms: an overlay, a drop-down cart, or an in-between page. The page says shoppers expect each form to support navigation toward their goal. Implication: pick one form and keep its controls reachable by keyboard.

cp-atc-gallery-split.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-atc-gallery-split.text: A confirmation-design index lists 175 desktop, 165 mobile and 24 app confirmation designs. Implication: desktop and mobile confirmations are the main variants a responsive component must cover; app confirmations are rarer.

cp-atc-gallery-visual.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-atc-gallery-visual.text: Looking at the page screenshot: a grid of about 364 small device-framed thumbnails of other sites' confirmation screens, with site name, device type and a count on each card, and an 'upgrade' badge over most of the cards. Implication: no visual pattern transfers from it; use the textual findings above.

cp-atc-aliases.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-atc-aliases.text: The same confirmation pattern is called added to basket, added to cart, or added to bag. Implication: pick one term for the bag and use it in the confirmation and the bag itself.

cp-container-queries.text: MDN defines container queries as styles applied to an element based on attributes of its container, set up with container-type of size, inline-size or normal. Implication: the card can switch its layout from its own width, so the same component works in grids and in a narrow bag drawer without media queries.

cp-system-ui.text: MDN says the system-ui generic family takes glyphs from the platform default user interface font, and that a font list lets the browser pick a fallback. Implication: a system font stack needs no webfont download and matches each device's own UI, with a generic sans-serif fallback at the end.

cp-title-link.text: The title is the only link. Heart, swatches and quick add are sibling buttons layered over the card, not nested inside the link, so no interactive control sits inside an anchor.

cp-swatch-overflow.text: In a narrow card the swatch row scrolls horizontally; the last swatch is cut off and the edge fades, so the shopper sees there are more colors.

cp-variant-one-card.text: One card per product, never one per color. Choosing a swatch updates price, badges and stock on the card and sets the link to the product page with the color selected.

cp-focus-path.text: Tab order: product link, then heart, then quick-add buttons, then each swatch. Focusing the card reveals the size row. Enter opens the product or adds the focused size; Space toggles the heart, picks the focused swatch or adds the focused size; Escape closes the sheet and returns focus to +.

cp-mobile-columns.text: Grid offers 2, 3 or 4 columns on wide screens; on phones a 2-column setting becomes 1 column and the others become 2. Recommendation rails instead scroll horizontally with snap points, each card about 176 px wide on phones and 224 px from the sm breakpoint.

cp-a11y-state.text: Sold-out sizes stay focusable with aria-disabled and an accessible name like 'sold out'. Selected swatch carries aria-pressed; wishlist heart uses aria-pressed; a polite live region announces saves and adds, and failures are announced as alerts.

cp-vs-selection-drives-price-media.term: selected variant drives price and image
cp-vs-selection-drives-price-media.text: Money and media components that reference selectedOrFirstAvailableVariant update automatically when a variant is selected. Implication: the price and the image follow the shopper's choice without extra wiring, so the bag and product card can show the chosen variant's values.

cp-swatch-pattern.text: Options can render as color swatches, each with its own label, selected and disabled parts. Fits colour-like options a shopper judges by sight, where a preview helps the choice (inferred from the markup, not stated by the page). Implication: each swatch needs a text label, so colour is never the only cue.

cp-radio-pattern.text: Options can render as radio options (radio, radio-selected and radio-disabled parts) inside the form. Styled as a row of buttons this reads as a segmented control, a name the page does not use. Fits a short list of text values such as sizes, where every choice stays visible on the screen.

cp-select-pattern.text: Options can render as a native select element (CSS part select). Fits a long option list or tight space (inferred; the page does not say when to use it). Trade-off: the other choices stay hidden until the shopper opens the menu, so a short list is better served by radio options.

cp-visible-option-split.text: The visible-option attribute shows one option per selector, and context.update(event) carries the selected options to another context. Fits a quick-add on a product card that shows one option, with the full chooser in a modal that shares the same selection.

cp-unavailable-option.text: Options unavailable for sale get their own disabled parts (radio-disabled, color-swatch-disabled), so they can look different from selectable options. Implication: keep unavailable options visible and marked rather than removing them.

cp-form-flex-layout.text: The form part has a flex layout, so a stylesheet can change the direction and gap of the whole selector through ::part(form). Implication: a row or column arrangement is a CSS choice, not a markup change.

cp-vs-form-in-product-context.text: The variant selector component (a store platform's web component) displays a form for selecting product options, and it must sit inside a product context. Implication: the selector belongs to the product it chooses for, so a card or a modal needs the same product context around it.

cp-size-buttons.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-size-buttons.text: Usability research recommends showing size options as buttons rather than inside a menu, because hidden sizes stop shoppers seeing what is available. Implication: unavailable sizes stay visible but marked, instead of hidden in a dropdown.

cp-stepper-default.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-stepper-default.text: Usability research notes that 1 is usually the default quantity when adding an item to a cart. Implication: the quantity starts at 1, and the stepper's minimum is 1, with removal handled by a separate control.

cp-stepper-variability.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-stepper-variability.text: Usability research says a stepper is poor for values with large variability, so a quantity stepper suits small whole counts. Implication: quantity steppers for carts, with a typed number field only when a large maximum is possible.

cp-add-sizes.term: size chips on hover or focus
cp-add-sizes.text: On the reference card a row of size buttons rises over the photo on pointer hover or keyboard focus, and sold-out sizes stay focusable and struck through. This component keeps the size row visible at rest, since hidden sizes stop shoppers seeing what is available (visible size buttons); the reveal is an observed option, not the rule.

cp-add-touch-sheet.text: On touch screens the reference card swaps the size row for a + button that opens a bottom sheet with the variant picker. This component keeps sizes visible at rest; the sheet is one option for narrow screens. Escape closes the sheet and returns focus to the + button.

cp-compare-at.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-compare-at.text: A sale display needs a compare-at price higher than the actual price. A common store platform shows the sale price at checkout, not the compare-at price. Implication: the card shows both, the bag and checkout show only the price paid.
cp-compare-at.never_implies: a compare-at price that was never a real recent price

cp-price-visible.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-price-visible.text: Listing guidance says the price stays permanently visible in product listings, and that universal attributes belong in every listing because they are essential to any product.

cp-sale-deterrent.rung: product card, quick-add, bag and checkout-handoff patterns
cp-sale-deterrent.text: Listing guidance on price-related offers says sales pricing can entice buyers, but unclear or inconsistent pricing information deters them. Implication: keep the sale, original and currency values consistent everywhere they appear.

look_and_feel._about: Values for the compact, minimal, modern shopping component: spacing, type, color roles with contrast-safe pairs, shape, and what the three adjectives permit. Standards values (target size, contrast, focus) are sourced in ux_principles; the rest are starting values (status illustrative), not requirements.

space._about: Spacing. Base 4 px. Starting values, status illustrative.

ls-space-scale.text: Start from these steps. Compact spacing sits between elements at 8 to 16 px; section rhythm uses 24 to 48 px. Off-scale values are fine when a layout needs one; keep them rare and documented.

ls-space-pad.text: Inner padding of the product card and bag line. 12 px is the compact default; 16 px when the card has room. Going below 12 px makes the text block cramped, so check legibility first.

ls-space-gap-cards.text: Gap between cards in a grid. The observed grid has a wide gutter; 16 px keeps the grid compact, 24 px when the image is the focus.

touch._about: Pointer target sizes in CSS px.

ls-target-comfort.text: The preferred size for the add button, quantity buttons and swatches on touch. 44 px is the WCAG 2.5.5 AAA figure, not an AA requirement; it is the comfort size to aim for, with 24 px as the hard floor.

ls-target-min.text: The WCAG 2.2 AA floor for pointer targets in the component: swatches, steppers, remove buttons, bag buttons, the add button. Smaller targets remain possible when spaced so that a 24 px circle around each one falls clear of its neighbours.

type._about: Type scale for the component. Sizes in px, line-height as a ratio. Starting values, status illustrative. Family: the default UI font, system-ui, sans-serif (see s-mdn-font-family).

ls-type-base.text: 16 px for body text and for every input, select and quantity field. Inputs under 16 px make some mobile browsers zoom on focus. Nothing in the component is set below 12 px.

ls-type-name.text: Product name: medium weight, one line, truncated with an ellipsis or wrapped to two lines at most.

ls-type-price.text: Price: semibold, tabular figures so that prices align in a list. It is the second-strongest text in the card after the product name; keep it at least as large as the name.

ls-type-meta.text: Meta text: color names, stock notes, tax note, shipping note. Uses the muted role; 12 px or larger.

color._about: Color roles for the default palette (Palette A, see options). Ratios were computed with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula. Text needs 4.5:1; controls and their state cues need 3:1 (SC 1.4.3 and 1.4.11, see ux_principles). Disabled controls are exempt, and are shown with reduced contrast plus a text label.

ls-role-ink.text: Product name, price, body text, selected variant label. Near-black; not pure black.

ls-role-muted.text: Meta text and secondary labels. Passes 4.5:1 on white with margin; do not use it on tinted surfaces without recomputing.

ls-role-accent.text: Add-to-bag button fill with white label (white on #1F5FBF is 6.09:1, passes 4.5:1), and the focus ring. Also usable as accent text on white at 6.09:1.

ls-role-border.text: Outline of inputs, quantity buttons and unselected swatches. Passes the 3:1 non-text rule (SC 1.4.11). Lighter grays such as #B3B3B3 (2.1:1) fail is a poor fit for a control's boundary.

ls-role-error.text: Out-of-stock and limit messages, and error text beside a field. Pair it with a text message and an icon or label, so color is not the only cue.

ls-role-ground.text: The card and bag background. Pure white by default. A tinted, warm or off-white card or bag surface is an allowed option when the text still passes 4.5:1 on it; the page behind may be any light ground.

shape._about: Radius, borders, elevation and focus. Starting values, status illustrative.

ls-radius.text: 8 px on buttons, inputs and swatches; 12 px at most on the card. One radius per kind of element, no nested radii.

ls-border-width.text: 1 px hairlines for dividers between bag lines and for control outlines. No double borders and no boxed frame around the whole component.

ls-focus-ring.text: Visible 2 px ring, 2 px offset, in the accent color: at least 3:1 against adjacent colors (SC 1.4.11) and shown on keyboard focus (SC 2.4.7). A sticky bag bar should leave a focused control visible (SC 2.4.11).

ls-elevation.text: Cards have no shadow at rest; separation comes from spacing and the hairline. The bag drawer or popover gets one shadow level, the one listed. Options: a soft shadow on card hover or focus for emphasis, or a faint lift on hover.

bindings._about: What each adjective binds to, and what it must not leak into.

ls-bind-compact.permits: gaps 8 to 16 px, card padding 12 to 16 px, one-line meta text, the stacked text block
never_implies: hiding the price or the add control

ls-bind-minimal.permits: removing ornament, extra badges and secondary copy that does not help the purchase
never_implies: blank or icon-only labels for add and bag
missing variant, quantity, price or checkout control
empty states without a next step

ls-bind-modern.permits: system-ui, CSS custom properties for the tokens above, flexible layout, container queries where the card sits in a variable-width slot

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where nothing in the prompt or the sources decides them. Pick one and state the choice; the ratios are computed the same way as above.

opt-palette-a.term: Palette A: neutral ink, one blue accent
opt-palette-a.text: Surface #FFFFFF, ink #1A1A1A (17.4:1), muted #595959 (7.0:1), accent #1F5FBF (6.09:1 with white label), control border #8A8A8A (3.45:1). Cool and plain; the default in this dump.

opt-palette-b.term: Palette B: warm paper, deep brown accent
opt-palette-b.text: Surface #FAFAF7, ink #1E1E1E (15.94:1), muted #5E5A54 (6.55:1 on #FAFAF7), accent #7A3E1D (7.92:1 as text on #FAFAF7, 8.29:1 as white label on it), control border #8A8478 (3.55:1 on #FAFAF7). Warmer and less clinical; recheck every pair if the surface changes.

opt-gradient-accent.term: gradient accent on the add button
opt-gradient-accent.text: Option: a subtle two-stop gradient on the add button, from the accent to a slightly darker accent. Tradeoff: more warmth and presence on the primary action, against more visual weight than the flat default and a contrast check at both stops, since the white label has to pass on the lighter one. The flat solid accent stays the default.

opt-trend-styles.text: Option: trend-led surfaces, such as glass panels, soft neumorphic wells or bento tiles. Tradeoff: a recognizable look and a sense of the present, against dating within a few seasons, lower text contrast on translucent grounds, and blur and shadow costs on older phones. The default is restrained system-level styling.

opt-phone-first.text: Reading of compact: a phone-first footprint, where the 390 px single-column card is the design and wider screens only add columns and room. Tradeoff: the tightest and most checked layout, against a plain desktop card with spare room. The default holds both sizes at once, so this reading is a choice of emphasis.

opt-raised-surfaces.text: Two labeled options. Option A, soft elevation: a faint shadow at rest such as 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.06) on the card. Tradeoff: clearer separation between cards, against visual noise in a grid and a shadow that some shoppers read as clutter. Option B, translucent drawer: a 92 percent white surface with a backdrop blur on the bag drawer only. Tradeoff: depth over the page, against text contrast that depends on what sits behind the drawer and a blur cost on low-end phones. Both sit beside the default: no shadow at rest and a solid drawer surface.

opt-tinted-ground.text: Option: a tinted surface of #F5F5F3 for the card or the bag instead of white. Recomputed on that ground with the WCAG relative-luminance formula: ink 15.9:1, muted 6.4:1, accent 5.6:1, border 3.2:1, error 6.0:1. All still clear their minimums, but the control border sits close to 3:1. Tradeoff: warmth and separation from a white page, against a thinner margin on the border and a recheck for every new tint. The pure white surface stays the default.

dec-currency-and-dark.text: Decision points for price formatting and the color scheme, each with a default.

decisions.default: Intl.NumberFormat with the store's currency code and the shopper's locale; two decimals; tabular figures on prices; the currency code is shown only where it differs from the page default

options.tradeoff: simple and predictable for one market, against wrong separators and symbols in other locales

decisions.default: light only, with color-scheme: light set on the root

options.tradeoff: matches the system setting and reads well at night, against a second palette to recheck. Values on the dark surface #151515: ink #F2F2F2 16.3:1, muted #B0B0B0 8.4:1, accent #8DB8FF used as a fill with label #151515 at 9.1:1, border #8F8F8F 5.7:1, error #FF8A80 8.0:1

lf-hexta-cards.text: Demo grid of two product cards on white: large near-square photos, a heart icon at the top right of each photo, and a row of small color dots under each photo. Text below is small and stacked (vendor, title, price, stars). The card reads by its photo first. Transfers: photo first, swatch row next, compact text stack, wide gutter between cards.
lf-hexta-cards.never_implies: the page's logo, its heart icon style or its Shopify code

lf-hexta-quickadd.term: quick add bar under the photo
lf-hexta-quickadd.text: A wide, pale rounded button sits below each product photo and above the text, labeled as quick add. It is a full-width control, not a small icon. Transfers: a full-width quick-add control placed between photo and text, visible at rest so the shopper does not need to hover to find it.
lf-hexta-quickadd.never_implies: that the button label or its pale fill is the brand's color

lf-hexta-density.text: The demo area is airy, with the cards spaced apart and one clear focus. The documentation below it is dense: stacked code blocks, tables with thin rules, and long text columns. Transfers: keep the component itself spacious and let the surrounding page carry the density, not the card.

lf-hexta-type.text: Black sans-serif text on white, gray for secondary lines, bold headings stepped in size, thin gray rules between table rows, code in light gray boxes with rounded corners. Transfers: one neutral text color, gray for secondary text, hairline dividers instead of boxes around the component.

lf-baymard-grid.text: Long four-column grid of phone-shaped and desktop-shaped thumbnails, each with a short caption (site and device). Uniform cell size; a few thumbnails carry a small dark pill badge. Overall the page is light gray with a dark navy footer. Transfers: a fixed grid of equal cells makes many states easy to compare at a glance; the eye reads shape and position before any text.
lf-baymard-grid.never_implies: what any single confirmation says, since the text is too small to read at this scale

lf-baymard-palette.text: Measured from the screenshot: light gray ground dominates, with a navy used for the footer and the badges.

lf-hexta-palette.text: Measured from the screenshot: near-white ground with a few light grays; ink is near-black.

component_anatomy._about: Parts of the compact shopping component in reading order, what each part does, what the minimal set holds, the default reading, and the alternatives as options. Derived from the research and pattern entries named in builds_on.

readings._about: Plausible readings of the request's scope. The default covers the whole job.

rd-default.term: product card with quick add and mini bag
rd-default.reading: product card with quick add, and a mini bag that reaches checkout
rd-default.text: Default reading: one card per product with quick add, plus a mini bag that reaches checkout. It covers the whole job end to end.

options._about: options, not requirements: alternative readings and anatomies where the request leaves the scope open

opt-reading-card-only.text: Option: a card with the add step and no bag or checkout. It stops at add, so the shopper reaches the bag through another page.

opt-reading-bag-only.reading: mini bag or bag drawer only (review, quantity, checkout)
opt-reading-bag-only.text: Option: a bag drawer alone, for a site where the product cards live elsewhere. It starts at the bag and ends at checkout.

opt-inline-bag.text: Option: a bag panel beside the card or in the page header instead of a drawer. It keeps the shopper in context and needs no overlay, but takes layout space and is harder to fit at phone width.

opt-quantity-omitted.text: Option: a product sold one per order drops the quantity stepper from the card. Add to bag adds 1, and the count appears in the bag. This shortens the card by one row.

opt-reading-browse-listing.term: product listing with filters and sort
opt-reading-browse-listing.text: Option: a browse listing, a grid of the same product cards with a filter panel and a sort control above the grid. Tradeoff: the component covers discovery as well as buying, against a much larger surface (filter state, empty results, URL sync) than one card and a bag. It stays out of the default reading; the card is its unit.

opt-icon-bag-aria.term: icon-only bag control with a stated count
opt-icon-bag-aria.text: Option: an icon-only bag control in the header, with a visible bag icon and an accessible name that states the count, for example 'Bag, 2 items' (aria-label or visually hidden text). Tradeoff: frees header space on narrow screens, against a control with no visible word that some shoppers will not recognize. The visible text label beside the icon stays the default; the k-cart-label check accepts an accessible name that states the count, so both pass.

opt-image-link.text: Option: the photo also links to the product page. Tradeoff: a larger click target and a familiar convention, against two links to one page; a screen reader announces both unless the photo link is hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden with tabindex -1) and the name carries the link. The default keeps the name as the link and the photo as an image.

dec-quantity-and-image.term: quantity placement and product image size
dec-quantity-and-image.text: Decision points for the quantity control and the photo frame, each with a default.

decisions.default: a stepper on the card starting at 1, with the count also changeable in the bag; add uses the card's quantity

options.option: add 1 from the card, change quantity in the bag
options.tradeoff: fewer controls on the card, against a second trip for a multi-item buy
the cleanest card, against no quantity choice before the add

decisions.default: a 1:1 frame at the width of the card column, cropped with object-fit: cover and supplied at 2x; the photo fills the single column at 390 px

options.tradeoff: product presence for garments and tall items, against taller cards and a longer grid
a middle ground for apparel, against more cropping of wide products

dec-data-and-deliverable.term: product data source and deliverable shape
dec-data-and-deliverable.text: Decision points for where the product data comes from and how the build is delivered, each with a default.

decisions.default: an inline JSON array in a script element, rendered by the same script

options.tradeoff: matches a live catalog and its loading states, against a loading and error path to build

options.option: data attributes on the card markup
options.tradeoff: one product with no script for data, against duplicating the data into every card

decisions.default: one HTML file with inline CSS and JS, so it opens from disk and is easy to review; split into three files when it is copied into a project

options.tradeoff: caching and editing in separate tools, against more files to keep in step

opt-image-ratio.text: Option: a 1:1 frame gives catalog uniformity and shorter cards, and the observed pages use near-square photos. A 4:5 frame gives the product more presence and makes the card taller, which pushes the price and add button lower in the viewport. Decision point: catalog uniformity versus product presence.

anat-name.text: Product name as text, one or two lines, and the card's only link to the product page. Its job is to identify the product and carry the link. Interactive controls such as the variant buttons and the add button sit beside the link, not inside it.

anat-price.text: Current price with the currency, directly under the name in the same group. On sale, the compare-at price sits struck through beside it, and the card shows both values with the same currency and format. The tax note stays out of the card and appears in the bag. Its job is to keep the price visible before any add step.
anat-price.never_implies: A sale badge does not replace the price. The sale and original values stay consistent everywhere they appear.

anat-quantity.text: A stepper with a minus button, the count, and a plus button, starting at 1. A stepper suits small whole counts, and a number input is the fallback for larger counts. Quantity is optional on the card. When the card leaves it out, add to bag adds 1, and the shopper changes the count in the bag.

anat-bag-count.text: A bag control with the item count, updated when an add succeeds. A polite live region announces the add, and a failed add is announced as an alert. Its job is to confirm the add happened and to give the shopper a way back to the bag.

anat-bag.text: Opens from the bag count as a drawer over the page, with a bag page as the fallback at small widths. Each line shows the image, name, variant, a quantity stepper, the line price and a remove control. Below the lines: the subtotal, and a note that tax and shipping are added at checkout. Its job is to review and change the bag before checkout.

anat-checkout.text: The bag's primary action, labeled with the checkout term, leads to the checkout page with the bag's items at the price paid. A text link beside it returns the shopper to browsing. The bag and checkout show the price paid, not the compare-at price. Its job is to hand the shopper to checkout with the same items and totals they saw in the bag.

anat-required.text: The parts a working minimal component holds: product name, price, add to bag, bag count, bag summary with lines and subtotal, and the checkout handoff. These six carry the whole job: find, see the price, add, see the bag, review it, check out. The photo is recommended and sits first.

anat-add.text: The primary action of the card: one full-width button labeled with the bag term (add to bag), placed after the price, quantity and variant choices. It keeps its width through pending (spinner), added and error states. An error message appears on the card where the shopper pressed. For a sold-out product the button is replaced by a Sold out badge and a notify link. Its job is to move the chosen variant and quantity into the bag.

anat-optional.text: Parts that can be left out of the minimal set: the variant picker (present when the product has variants, absent when it does not), the quantity stepper on the card (add 1 and change in the bag), the compare-at price (present when on sale), the sold-out badge (present when stock is tracked), the swatch overflow fade (present when colors exceed the card width), and the second hover image.

anat-image.text: The photo leads the card in a fixed-ratio frame (1:1 by default) so cards in a row line up. The name is the one link by default. A photo that links to the same product page is an allowed option, marked hidden from the tab order so the card keeps one tab stop. Its job is to show the product, so the shopper knows what they are choosing. Alt text names the product and the selected color when one is chosen.

anat-variant.text: Present when the product has variants: a row of size buttons, or a row of color swatches, placed between the price and the add button. A product with a single variant has no picker, and the add button sits directly under the price. Each option is a real button with its name as the accessible name. A sold-out option stays focusable, is struck through, and is marked as sold out.

anat-order.text: Reading order from top to bottom: product image, product name, price, variant picker (present when the product has variants), quantity (optional), add to bag. The bag summary and the checkout action sit in a separate bag surface reached from the bag count. Each part is its own element, and the name is the card's link to the product page. The observed reference card lists photo, badges, quick add, swatches, vendor, title, price, rating; this component keeps the first, the title, the price and the controls, and drops the rest.

states_and_flow._about: Interaction states, add-to-bag feedback, motion timings, labels, the 390 px layout and the keyboard path for the shopping component. No watch job or video was found, so no timeline entries exist. Every duration here is inferred (no fetched source gives a timing for these states); treat the ms values as starting points to tune, not measurements.

states._about: Each control's states. Researched entries come from the HextaUI product card and WCAG 2.2 pages; the rest are inferred.

st-hover-press.text: Hover changes the button background by one step in its color role. Pressed scales the button to 0.98 for the press and returns it on release. Both are decoration: no information is carried by hover alone.
st-hover-press.never_implies: a bounce or overshoot on press

st-focus-visible.text: WCAG 2.2 requires a visible keyboard focus indicator (2.4.7), with at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors (1.4.11), and a focused control not entirely hidden by a sticky header or the bag drawer (2.4.11). A 2 px ring offset 2 px is an inferred starting width; the sources give no pixel value.
st-focus-visible.never_implies: removing the ring for a cleaner look

st-error.text: On failure the label becomes 'Couldn't add' on the same card where the shopper clicked, with the message from the failed request if one is returned. The failure is announced as an alert. The control returns to its enabled state so the shopper can try again.

st-empty-bag.text: An empty bag shows the line 'Your bag is empty' with one link back to shopping and no checkout action. The bag count reads 0 or is omitted; pick one and keep it the same everywhere the count appears.

st-added.text: On success the label becomes 'Added' for a short hold, the bag count rises, and a polite live region announces the item with its selected options (a reference card announces 'Added <product>, <variant> to your bag'). The label then returns to 'Add to bag'.

st-disabled.text: The add control is disabled only when a reason exists (no variant chosen, or the chosen variant is out of stock), and the reason is written beside it in text. Use aria-disabled rather than the disabled attribute so the control stays focusable and its reason can be reached, matching the reference card's sold-out size pattern.
st-disabled.never_implies: a greyed-out look with no explanation

st-pending.text: While the add request runs, the button keeps its width and shows a spinner in place of its label. The rest of the card stays usable. The button reads as busy to assistive tech (aria-busy on the control or its region, inferred).

st-rest.term: rest state of the add control
st-rest.text: The add-to-bag control is visible at rest on every card, including touch screens. Hover adds emphasis; touch and keyboard users reach add without hover.
st-rest.never_implies: a control that appears only on pointer hover

st-sold-out.text: Product-level out of stock, when every variant is out: the default keeps the add control visible and focusable as aria-disabled, with 'Sold out' written beside it and a 'Notify me' link when restock alerts exist (the default in dec-states). The reference card removes the control and shows a Sold out badge instead; that is an option. Size-level out of stock: the size stays in the row, struck through, focusable with aria-disabled, and named 'sold out' for screen readers.

motion._about: Timings in ms. All inferred: no fetched source gives these values. Use them as a first pass and tune by eye on a real device.

mo-label-swap.text: The add label cross-fades to 'Added' or 'Couldn't add' in 150 ms ease-out, holds for 1500 ms, then cross-fades back to 'Add to bag'. The announcement is carried by the live region, not by the animation.

mo-count-bump.text: The bag count rises from 1.0 to 1.15 scale and returns in 200 ms ease-out, once per successful add. The number changes at once; only the scale animates.

mo-drawer.text: The bag drawer slides in from the right in 240 ms ease-out and out in 180 ms ease-in; on a 390 px screen it rises as a bottom sheet over the same timings. Exit is faster than entry so dismissal feels immediate.

mo-reduced.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3 lets interaction-triggered motion be disabled. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the drawer and the bag count drop their slide and scale and change at once (0 ms), and the label swap keeps only an opacity change of 0 ms. The drawer still opens and closes; only its movement is removed.

labels._about: Labels the component shows. Lexicon-level choices: one term for the bag used everywhere (Baymard lists Added to Cart, Added to Basket and Added to Bag as aliases of one pattern).

lx-add.text: The add label. Use 'Add to bag' with the bag term in every label on the component.

lx-error.text: The failure label. Apostrophe as typed; the next step is a retry, so keep the control enabled beside it.

lx-bag.text: The bag noun, with the count in a badge (for example 'Bag, 2 items'). Pick this term over Cart or Basket and use it everywhere.

lx-added.text: The success label on the add control. Single word, the usual choice on reference cards.

lx-checkout.text: The checkout action in the bag. Plain 'Checkout' with the subtotal beside it; the label names the destination, as the usability finding on labels requires.

lx-sold-out.text: The out-of-stock badge. 'Notify me' is the link beside it when the product can notify the shopper of restock; reference cards use both together.

lx-view-bag.text: The label on the after-add link to the bag. Usability testing found vague labels make shoppers hunt for the way on, so name the destination exactly.

flow._about: The path a shopper takes through select, add, bag and checkout, and the layout at 390 px.

kb-select-add-bag.text: Tab order: product title link, then the variant or size radio group (one tab stop; arrow keys move within it), then Add to bag, then the Bag button in the header. Enter or Space on Add to bag adds the chosen variant. The bag opens on Enter or Space on the Bag button. Focus moves to the drawer heading on open. Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to the Bag button. Focus stays on Add to bag after an add, and the live region carries the announcement.

fl-drawer-focus.text: While the drawer is open, Tab keeps focus inside it, so the page behind stays out of the tab order. The drawer's close button is reachable and labeled. Closing restores focus to the element that opened it. A sticky header should stay clear of the drawer's controls (WCAG 2.4.11).

fl-mobile-390.text: At 390 px the grid is one column: the card's image, then its title and price, then the variant row, then Add to bag at full width. Touch targets are at least 24 px per WCAG 2.5.8; 44 px is an inferred comfort size for thumbs, not a sourced minimum. Multi-option variant pickers open in a bottom sheet (reference pattern) instead of an expanded row. Side gutter 16 px is inferred.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the sources are silent

opt-bag-390.text: Option: at 390 px, open the bag as a full page instead of a bottom sheet. Tradeoff: more room for the review and checkout action on a small screen, against losing the browsing context a sheet keeps.

opt-checkout-failure.text: Option: before the checkout handoff, recheck stock and price for each bag line. A changed price or a sold-out line returns the shopper to the bag, with that line marked and a text message in the error color. If checkout fails after the handoff, the checkout page returns the shopper to the bag with the message. Tradeoff: no dead ends and no surprise totals, against one extra request before checkout and the work of a message and a retry path. The default is the plain link handoff with no recheck (see dec-bag-controls), so this option is the upgrade path.

opt-bag-persist.text: Option: the bag survives a reload, through the store's server session (a cookie, the usual choice for a live store) or through localStorage in a prototype with no server. Tradeoff: a returning shopper finds their items, against stale prices and stock, a storage choice to make, and questions about what is kept on the device. The default holds the bag in the server session and keeps no client storage, so a reload restores the bag only where that session does.

opt-undo-remove.term: undo after removing a bag line
opt-undo-remove.text: Option: removing a line shows a short notice beside the bag, 'Removed Linen Shirt. Undo', for about 5 seconds, and Undo restores the line with its quantity. Tradeoff: recovery from an accidental remove, against a timer to build, a live region to announce the notice, and a removed line that sits in limbo for a few seconds. Keep the notice long enough to read and reachable by keyboard (WCAG 2.2.1, timing adjustable). The default removes the line at once with no undo; the shopper re-adds it from the card.

dec-states.text: Decision points for the add control and the count, each with a default.

decisions.default: aria-disabled add control with the reason 'Sold out' written beside it, plus a Notify me link when restock alerts exist; the control stays in the tab order. This changes st-sold-out, which removes the control, for the case where every variant is out

options.option: removed control with a Sold out badge (the st-sold-out wording)
options.tradeoff: a clean card, against no control for the reason to attach to and no focus target for a keyboard reader
a plain disabled state, against removing the control from the tab order so the reason is hard to reach by keyboard

decisions.default: the plus button disables at the limit; text in the error color beside the count reads 'Only 3 left' when stock is the cause and 'Limit 10 per order' when the per-order cap is (the numbers are placeholders)

options.tradeoff: fewest words, against a shopper who thinks the button broke
a message after the press, against a failed action the shopper had to attempt

decisions.default: the count badge is hidden at zero, and the bag button's accessible name ends with 'empty'

options.tradeoff: a steady header and an explicit zero, against a number that carries no news and adds noise

dec-motion-and-breakpoints.term: press under reduced motion and breakpoints
dec-motion-and-breakpoints.text: Decision points for the press effect and the layout widths, each with a default.

decisions.default: scale 0.98 applies only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; under reduce, a pressed control shows the color step alone

options.tradeoff: the simplest CSS with no media query for it, against less tactile feedback on touch

decisions.default: one column to 599 px, two columns from 600 px, three from 900 px and four from 1200 px; the bag is a bottom sheet below 600 px and a side drawer from 600 px

options.tradeoff: room to review and check out on a phone, against a page change that loses the product context
one pattern to build and test, against a sheet that looks cramped on wide screens

dec-bag-controls.term: bag line remove control and checkout handoff
dec-bag-controls.text: Decision points for the controls inside the bag, each with a default.

decisions.default: a visible text button 'Remove' whose accessible name adds the line's item, for example 'Remove Linen Shirt, size M', with the item part visually hidden

options.tradeoff: a clean row, against a control with no visible word

options.option: text Remove with no item in the name
options.tradeoff: the name matches the sight label exactly, against several identical Remove buttons in a list for a screen reader user

decisions.default: a plain link styled as the primary button, to the checkout URL; the bag rides in the server session, with no client script

options.tradeoff: sends the bag in the request, against a form to build and a page that reloads on error

options.option: script callback that fetches, then navigates
options.tradeoff: can recheck stock before the move, against a path that can fail and a control that does nothing without script
full control of the payment step inside the page, against focus and accessibility issues and frame-embedding restrictions from payment providers

lexicon._about: Vocabulary to draw on for copy, markup and pitch. Inferred from how shops and designers talk about these qualities; candidate wording, not requirements.

search_vocabulary._about: Candidate vocabulary for search titles, descriptions and alt text. Candidate wording, not checked against search demand.

sv-short.text: Candidate vocabulary: short phrases for titles and tags.

sv-medium.term: compact product card with quick add
variants: product card with variant picker and quantity stepper
sv-medium.text: Candidate vocabulary: medium phrases for descriptions and headings.

sv-long.term: compact minimal product card with variant picker, quantity stepper and added-to-bag feedback
variants: modern shopping component with mini bag and checkout button for mobile web
responsive add to bag component with keyboard focus and reduced motion
sv-long.text: Candidate vocabulary: long-tail phrases for alt text and detailed descriptions.

lx-compact.text: Compact in shop and design talk means a small footprint with few parts, spacing that is tight but comfortable to read, and controls that stay easy to hit. People say a compact layout fits the card or sits neatly, not that it looks squeezed.

lx-minimal.text: Minimal in product design talk means few elements, little ornament, and each part earning its place. Shoppers read it as calm and easy to scan. It describes restraint in what is shown, not an empty or unlabeled interface.

lx-modern.text: Modern in web talk means current conventions: a system font stack or a clean sans, flexible layout, clear hierarchy, restrained color and standard controls. It reads as current and unfussy, not as a passing visual trend.

lx-buying-flow.text: The steps from seeing a product to paying for it. In UX talk a clear buying flow is short, shows the price and the choices up front, confirms each action, and gives a way back.

lx-product-card.text: A repeated unit in a product grid: image, name, price and one next action. Its feel comes from the image ratio, a short name, a single clear price line and one primary control.

lx-quick-add.text: A control on the product card that adds the default variant to the bag without opening the product page. Shoppers use it for fast repeat choices. It needs a visible confirmation and a path to change options.

lx-quantity-stepper.text: A minus button, a count and a plus button for choosing quantity. Its feel comes from buttons large enough to hit, a count that announces its change, a floor at one and a ceiling when stock is limited.

lx-price-line.text: The price as shoppers read it: the current price in the largest type, an earlier price struck through when on sale, the currency shown plainly, and a short tax or shipping note close by.

associations._about: Associated people, works and practices, and mood words. Seed material that widens the work; tier 3 for named practices, tier 4 for pools. Names stay here, not in the descriptions a consumer reuses.

as-less-but-better.text: The industrial design principle associated with Dieter Rams: reduce a product to its essentials and keep it honest and unobtrusive. Contributes: remove a control before adding a decoration, and let the product lead, not the chrome.

as-ma.text: The Japanese design concept of meaningful interval: empty space that gives the elements around it weight. Contributes: spacing as a deliberate tool, which keeps a compact component from feeling crowded.

as-swiss-typography.text: Sans-serif type on a strict grid with clear size contrast and flush-left text, associated with mid-century Swiss graphic design. Contributes: a type hierarchy built from size and weight rather than color or ornament, for product name, price and meta text.

as-plain-retail-labeling.text: Neutral palettes and plain labels in everyday retail, associated with a Japanese household goods brand. Contributes: a near-neutral base where the product image carries the color.

as-storefront-conventions.text: Stores built on common themes share a product card with image, name, price and one primary button. Contributes: the layout shoppers already expect, which lowers the cost of learning the component.

as-modular-grid.text: A grid of modular tiles of varied size, common in current web layouts. Contributes: one layout option for a product grid or a bag summary, not a requirement for the component.

as-mood-pool.text: A pool of mood words for how the component should feel: crisp, tidy, settled, exact. Sample a couple for variety. These are tone words, not visual facts.
